stations.title: Rooftop Material Segmentation from Drone Imagery
stations.summary: Engineered deep learning segmentation pipelines classifying rooftop materials across 17,954 building footprints using high-resolution drone imagery.
highlights: Trained multi-spectral U-Net and DeepLabV3+ segmentation architectures on drone aerial orthomosaics spanning 17,954 building polygons.
Classified thatch, corrugated metal, concrete, and ceramic tile with 91.4% mIoU accuracy under extreme illumination variation.
Extracted spatial socio-economic vulnerability indicators for automated humanitarian disaster resilience mapping.

qa.question: Why was semantic segmentation on drone imagery challenging?
qa.answer: Extreme shadow angles, reflective metallic glare, and irregular informal settlement roof boundaries required specialized data augmentation and dice-focal loss tuning.

qa.question: What dataset and volume of buildings were processed?
qa.answer: Processed high-resolution aerial drone ortho-imagery categorizing 17,954 building footprints across Nacala, Mozambique by roofing material.

qa.question: What accuracy metrics were achieved?
qa.answer: Achieved a 91.4% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) score using PyTorch convolutional segmentation pipelines with custom loss functions.

qa.question: What was the real-world humanitarian application?
qa.answer: The classifications assisted disaster response planners and municipal agencies in identifying cyclone-vulnerable informal roofing structures before monsoon seasons.

challenges.title: Severe 56:1 Class Imbalance
challenges.realityAndContext: In dense informal settlements, corrugated metal sheet roofs heavily dominate the terrain (9,776 buildings) while high-vulnerability materials like concrete (174) and asbestos (394) are rare.
challenges.theObstacle: Standard Binary Cross-Entropy loss treated rare building materials as statistical noise and collapsed into predicting the dominant metal class for every structure.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Mathematically formulated a dual-head hybrid loss combining class-weighted focal loss with soft Dice coefficients, explicitly penalizing rare-class misclassifications over background.
challenges.outcomeMetric: 0.867 IoU benchmark achieved across 17,954 annotated structures

challenges.title: Touching Buildings in Dense Informal Settlements
challenges.realityAndContext: Informal settlement structures are built so close together that their rooftops physically touch, making it difficult for public health mappers to count distinct dwellings.
challenges.theObstacle: Standard semantic segmentation models merge touching polygons into single large blobs, completely failing building instance counting.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Engineered a Deep Ordinal Watershed (DOW) architecture with dual heads: one head predicts semantic material masks while the second predicts instance boundary separation gradients.
challenges.outcomeMetric: Zero polygon merging across touching rooftop clusters

stations.title: Intelligent Seismic Activity Detection: Deep Learning Approach
stations.summary: Sole primary author on peer-reviewed research accepted and presented at SME-2025 (IIT ISM Dhanbad), benchmarking deep neural network cross-region transferability across Southern California, Chile, and Hindukush seismic catalogs.
highlights: Authored peer-reviewed paper 'Intelligent Seismic Activity Detection: A Deep Learning Approach' accepted & presented at SME-2025 (IIT ISM Dhanbad).
Formulated geophysical feature extraction incorporating Gutenberg-Richter a/b values, energy release rates, recurrence intervals, and magnitude deficits for M > 5.0 forecasting.
Achieved 99.05% in-sample accuracy and systematically benchmarked multi-regime cross-transferability across 3 disparate tectonic catalogs.

qa.question: What was the core research problem explored in the SME-2025 paper?
qa.answer: Investigated whether deep neural networks for earthquake forecasting generalize across tectonically disparate regimes (Southern California, Chile, Hindukush) or overfit regional catalog idiosyncrasies.

qa.question: What geophysical features were extracted for modeling?
qa.answer: Derived Gutenberg-Richter a and b values, cumulative seismic energy release rates, recurrence time intervals, and magnitude deficits to forecast major events (M > 5.0).

qa.question: Where was this research presented and accepted?
qa.answer: Peer-reviewed and presented at the International Conference on Sustainable Mining & Energy (SME-2025), hosted by the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad.

qa.question: What were the key quantitative findings?
qa.answer: Demonstrated 99.05% in-sample detection accuracy while discovering concrete cross-region transferability bounds between continental strike-slip faults and subduction zones.

challenges.title: Cross-Region Tectonic Transferability vs Catalog Overfitting
challenges.realityAndContext: Seismic catalogs differ dramatically across fault mechanisms (strike-slip in California vs subduction in Chile vs deep mantle in Hindukush).
challenges.theObstacle: Deep models trained on a single catalog achieved high in-sample metrics but degraded significantly when transferred across different tectonic stress regimes.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Standardized feature engineering with Gutenberg-Richter parameterization and energy release rates, benchmarking transfer gaps to quantify regime-specific variance.
challenges.outcomeMetric: 99.05% in-sample accuracy and multi-regime transferability evaluation

challenges.title: The Ephemeral Free-Tier Container Challenge
challenges.realityAndContext: Cloud containers on platforms like Render go to sleep after 15 minutes of user inactivity and wipe local storage upon every restart and deployment.
challenges.theObstacle: A standalone SQLite database loses all registered user accounts and expense logs on server reboot, while making remote cloud database calls introduces sluggish network latency.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Engineered a Two-Phase Cold-Start Hydration pipeline: Phase 1 synchronously pulls active metadata and 2,000 transactions in <300ms for sub-second server boot, while Phase 2 streams older historical records in the background, paired with write-through Turso cloud persistence and a durable local outbox.
challenges.outcomeMetric: Render health check boots in <1 second with 100% durable cloud persistence

challenges.title: Cross-Origin Third-Party Cookie Blocking
challenges.realityAndContext: Modern privacy engines in Safari, Firefox, and Chrome block third-party cross-site cookies between decoupled origins (*.vercel.app frontend and *.onrender.com backend).
challenges.theObstacle: Storing authentication in httpOnly cookies resulted in silent session dropouts for users unless paying for custom unified apex domain routing.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Architected authentication using client-side JWTs in Authorization: Bearer headers, protected by Angular's strict DomSanitizer and offline-first PWA inspection.
challenges.outcomeMetric: Flawless offline-first airplane-mode hydration with zero cross-site cookie drops

challenges.title: LiDAR Clutter in Bare-Earth DTM Generation
challenges.realityAndContext: Under the national SVAMITVA Scheme, planning rural rainwater drainage requires clean elevation data, but raw drone LiDAR scans capture everything from rooftops to tree canopies.
challenges.theObstacle: Surface clutter distorts terrain elevation gradients, causing classical hydrology models to predict water flowing uphill or pooling over house roofs.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Implemented a PointNet-style ground-filtering regression model (TerrainNet) that strips all vegetation and structures to extract a pure Digital Terrain Model (DTM) before running D8 flow-routing simulations.
challenges.outcomeMetric: Accurate watershed delineation across 6 surveyed Indian village clusters

challenges.title: Small Utility Detection Imbalance in Drone Orthophotos
challenges.realityAndContext: Rural infrastructure maps require spotting critical small utilities (transformers, wells, overhead tanks) alongside massive roads and building clusters.
challenges.theObstacle: Utility points occupy under 0.05% of orthophoto pixels, causing detectors to miss them completely in favor of vast building and road masks.
challenges.decisionAndTradeoff: Pioneered a 3-model semantic segmentation ensemble (SegFormer + Mask2Former + dual-attention U-Net++) with class-specific confidence thresholds and minimum pixel cluster validation.
challenges.outcomeMetric: Selected Top 10% (40 out of 400 national teams) by IIT Tirupati & MoPR
